parsed.stack: iOS + Android (React Native). Entirely on-device for the drill - playback of the grandmother's own recorded audio plus an on-device model for prompts, $0 marginal. Small cloud text calls only for Punjabi/Gujarati transliteration and phrase curation, where on-device models are genuinely weak. Recordings stored locally with encrypted backup. Freemium subscription.
milestones: Week 1-2: guided recording flow for the grandmother (she is 75 and not the app user - this has to work over a phone call or a visit, in one sitting).
Week 3-4: the fixed 50-phrase Sunday-call curriculum for Punjabi and Gujarati, with Gurmukhi/Gujarati script rendering and a Latin transliteration that native speakers do not wince at.
Week 5-6: on-device spaced repetition tied to the real Sunday call, not an arbitrary daily streak.
Week 7: freemium gate (first 15 phrases free), plus the community embed - a shareable deck for cousins with the same grandmother.
Week 8: 20 second-generation users recruited through British Punjabi and Gujarati community pages.
parsed.riskiest_technical_assumption: That models handle Punjabi and Gujarati - including dialect, Gurmukhi/Shahmukhi script choice and transliteration - well enough that the 50 phrases are not subtly wrong, because a native-speaking grandmother is the harshest possible QA and a single wrong phrase discredits the whole deck.
parsed.cheapest_way_to_test_that_assumption: Pay two native speakers (one Punjabi, one Gujarati) about £300 each to review a generated 50-phrase deck line by line before any code is written.
